newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa adds 339 mln rand to 1997/98 spending.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa adds 339 mln rand to 1997/98 spending.

text.p: South African Deputy Minister of Finance Gill Marcus on Thursday tabled a supplementary budget estimate of 339 million rand, which was marginally lower than the amount previewed in the March 12 budget speech.
The supplementary estimate formalises spending proposed in the main 1997/98 budget, but calculated too late to be included in the government's formal spending proposals on budget day.

The amounts, already reflected in Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's 186.7 billion rand spending proposals, include 337.2 million rand for state salary increases, 175 million rand for welfare payments and 226.8 million rand for a new teaching hospital in Durban.

A proposed saving of 400 million rand from the reduction in state pension contributions from 18 pct to 17 pct of salaries is offset against the total proposed additional spending of 739 million for a net increase of 339 million rand.
The increase is 200,000 rand lower than the amount anticipated in Manuel's budget speech because of a slight reduction in the estimated cost of the Durban hospital.
The supplementary estimate was introduced in parliament on Thursday, but set down for debate at a later date.
